cards.title: The IK spider boss
cards.text: Your test boss: a body held up on six IK legs, stomps, a head slam with a stun on a miss, legs that break. 0.32.0.
cards.why: Try it in battle mode (the new 'No dungeon yet' tab) or the Book. Mark any part that's off; the calls are the cards after.

parts.title: Body and legs
parts.text: A plum spider four heroes long: bone face plate, fangs, four ember eyes, an hourglass. The body is up in the air, so only shots reach it and heroes walk under it; one shadow on the floor. Six legs with knees bent up, stepping in two alternating sets of three; feet stay planted until they step.

parts.title: Stomp
parts.text: A red circle at a hero, the leg lifts straight up and stabs down: a dent and dust. The foot sticks a moment after.

parts.title: Head slam
parts.text: Its eyes flare and a circle follows under it as it walks, then a split-second stop and the drop. On a miss it lies stunned on the floor about a second (longer per broken leg) and everyone can hit it.

parts.title: Breaking legs
parts.text: Each foot has its own health; blades go for the feet. A broken leg turns grey and drags with its knee on the floor, can't stomp, slows it and lengthens the stun. Four broken: it collapses and fights from the floor, dragging itself, slamming from its belly.

parts.title: Extra moves
parts.text: Web spit: a ball arcs at a hero and holds them in web for 1.5 s (or leaves a web patch). Brood: spiderlings come down from under it, more in phase 2. At 60% health it hisses and gets quicker.

parts.title: How hard
parts.text: At level 25 (the third boss's level) it's about as hard as the Great Ooze for a standard party and easier for blade-heavy ones. Health is the knob if you want it harder.

cards.title: Knee height
cards.text: Knees sit at a third of their real height so the front legs don't cover its face. Keep?
cards.why: At full height it looks leggier but hides the face.

cards.title: Spiderlings from the start
cards.text: It drops one spiderling at a time from the start of the fight (two in phase 2). Keep?
cards.why: With none a standard party won every time; with two at once it won 6 in 20.

cards.title: Its name
cards.text: Working name: Old Longlegs. Keep or rename?
cards.why: It's a test boss for now; the name can wait until it gets a dungeon.
